subject: Advance commitment proposal — 2yr escalator & SKU bucketing
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@harpoon.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Advance commitment proposal — initial runbook and escalator idea

Hi Olivia,

Great chatting yesterday — appreciate the context on Harpoon's 2027 roadmap. Based on the volume ranges you mentioned for Q2–Q4, I sketched an advance-commit approach that balances discounted unit economics with flexibility during the ramp. Key points (summary):

- Structure: 2-year advance commitment with annual true-ups (6-month cadence optional).
- Ramp buckets: Year 1 staged allocation (50% / 75% / 100% monthly cadence) that converts unused allocation into discounted overage credits.
- Price: Baseline list with an escalator discount schedule tied to committed tiers (see attached ROI model).
- Ops: Redwood will guarantee dedicated capacity windows for your monthly peaks; fallback models available if you exceed headroom.

I've attached a simple ROI workbook showing breakpoints and an initial SOW stub for scope. Can you confirm: (1) whether Harpoon needs invoice split across fiscal quarters, and (2) if a 6-month true-up cadence would be acceptable?

If that sounds close, I can loop in Finance & Legal to get a formal SOW and a DocuSign-ready paper.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Harpoon_ROI_Model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), RDW_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@harpoon.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Advance commitment proposal — initial runbook and escalator idea

Marcus — thanks for the write-up and the ROIs. A few questions from our side:

1) For the ramp buckets — if we underutilize in Q1 of Year 1, how does conversion to credits actually work (on invoice or account balance)?
2) We need a net-60 payment term on any advance invoice and prefer split invoices across quarters for our accounting. Is that supported?
3) Regarding the escalator: can you confirm whether the discount applies to all tokens across the month once a breakpoint is hit or just to additional usage after the breakpoint?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@harpoon.ai) — they will want a copy of the SOW and high-level SLAs.

— Olivia
VP Product, Harpoon.ai
olivia.grant@harpoon.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Advance commitment proposal — initial runbook and escalator idea

Ben / Monica / Steph — fyi, Harpoon responded with the questions below. Key asks: net-60, split invoices across quarters, clarification on how escalator applies, and conversion of underutilization into credits.

Can Finance/legal comment on feasibility of:
- Net-60 on advance invoice (we usually do net-30 for new deals, but Harpoon is a strategic target).
- Allowing quarter-split invoicing for advance payment (yes/no and operational overhead).
- Approval to structure the escalator so that when a monthly breakpoint is hit, the breakpoint discount applies retroactively to the entire month's committed usage (this materially helps their forecast).

I've attached the ROI model and draft SOW for context. I'd like to propose: 2-year advance commitment, year-1 staged allocation (50/75/100), discounted table with 10% / 15% / 20% breakpoints depending on committed tier. If Finance/legal sign off, I'll send a formal offer.

—Marcus

Attachments: Harpoon_ROI_Model_v3.xlsx, RDW_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Advance commitment proposal — initial runbook and escalator idea

Marcus — good call on bringing finance in early. Quick thoughts:

- Net-60: Acceptable as an exception for strategic accounts if Sales gets approval from Revenue Ops and Deal Desk. I'll prepare a short exception rationale.
- Split invoicing across quarters: Operationally doable but we should limit to 4 invoices per year max and flag the account for manual AR reconciliation. Recommend we add an admin fee of $2,500 per year to cover extra billing effort (negotiable).
- Escalator retroactivity: OK to offer retroactive discount for the month once a breakpoint is hit, but limit it to three retroactive months in Year 1 for accounting simplicity. After Year 1, retroactivity can be monthly.

Suggested offer for internal approval:
- 2-year advance commit (annualized), tiered discounts by committed TPUs: 10% (>250M TPU), 15% (>500M TPU), 22% (>1B TPU).
- Year-1 ramp buckets: 50% / 75% / 100% monthly cadence. Unused committed units convert to account credit at 60% of list price and can be applied to overages or next-term true-ups.
- Payment: one advance invoice per year (split option per customer request), net-60 with Deal Desk exception, $2,500 billing admin fee if split across 2+ invoices per year.

If that sounds reasonable I'll draft the approval note for Steph to sign off. Ben
Account Director | Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 13:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Advance commitment proposal — initial runbook and escalator idea

Ben/Team — I approve the exception with the following firm conditions:

1) Net-60 approved for Year 1 only; Year 2 reverts to standard net-30 unless AR risk is low after the first true-up.
2) Billing admin fee is fine — include it as a one-line item in the SOW.
3) Retroactivity: allow up to three retroactive months in Year 1; after that, retroactivity monthly as Ben recommended.
4) Add a 6-month true-up clause and a cap: if overages exceed 30% of committed units in any quarter, Redwood reserves right to invoke capacity rebalancing or require an uplift.

Once Legal attaches the SOW language for the true-up and the overage cap, Marcus go ahead and send the formal offer to Harpoon with the DocuSign link.

—Steph
VP Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@harpoon.ai>, Procurement <procurement@harpoon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Formal offer: 2-year advance commitment with escalator (DocuSign link)

Hi Olivia / Harpoon procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on questions. Per our internal approvals, please find the formal offer below:

Summary of material terms
- Term: 2 years (annualized billing with option to split invoices across fiscal quarters at customer request).
- Commitment: Annual advance commitment with Year-1 ramp buckets (50%/75%/100%).
- Pricing & Discounts: Tiered discounts by committed TPU: 10% / 15% / 22% as outlined in the attached ROI model. Once a monthly breakpoint is reached, the breakpoint discount will be applied retroactively for up to three months in Year 1 and monthly thereafter.
- Payment: Net-60 for Year 1 (Deal Desk exception), standard net-30 in Year 2 unless otherwise agreed after true-up. Billing admin fee of $2,500 if invoices are split across quarters.
- Credits & Overages: Unused committed units in Year 1 convert to account credit at 60% of list price; credits may be used for overages or applied to next-term true-up. Overages beyond 30% of committed units in any quarter trigger capacity rebalancing or uplift discussions.
- Ops & SLA: Redwood will provide dedicated capacity windows and an SLA consistent with our Dedicated plan; fallback to compatible model variants if we hit platform constraints (detailed in SOW).

Attachments: RDW_Draft_SOW_v2.pdf (Legal language updated), Harpoon_ROI_Model_v4.xlsx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/sign?token=abc123xyz

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement to confirm invoice split preference and PO flow.
2) Sign SOW via DocuSign.
3) Redwood to issue Year-1 advance invoice on agreed schedule (we will allow one split across fiscal quarters if requested).

Olivia — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the ramp buckets and how credits would be applied.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: RDW_Draft_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), Harpoon_ROI_Model_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet)
